{{Current events|year=2022|month=01|day=31|content=
<!-- All news items below this line -->
'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*Spillover of the [[Somali Civil War (2009–present)|Somali Civil War]]
**Thirteen people are killed after a bus hit a [[Improvised explosive device|roadside bomb]] planted by suspected [[Al-Shabaab (militant group)|Al-Shabaab]] militants in [[Mandera]], [[Kenya]], near the border with [[Somalia]]. [https://www.voanews.com/a/roadside-bomb-hits-bus-on-kenya-somalia-border/6419840.html (VOA)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2022 Brazil floods and landslides]]
**[[Flash flood]]ing and landslides caused by torrential rains kill at least 19 people and leave hundreds more [[homeless]] in the [[Brazilian state]] of [[São Paulo (state)|São Paulo]]. This brings the total death toll from flooding in the country to more than 50 people since the start of the [[wet season]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-latin-america-60197978 (BBC News)]
*[[2022 Ecuador landslides]]
**At least 23 people are killed in and 47 injured in landslides in [[Quito]], [[Ecuador]]. [https://edition.cnn.com/2022/02/01/americas/ecuador-landslide-intl-latam/index.html (CNN)]
'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in North America]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Canada]]
****[[Prime Minister of Canada|Prime minister]] [[Justin Trudeau]] tests positive for [[COVID-19]]. [https://www.thestar.com/politics/federal/2022/01/31/prime-minister-justin-trudeau-says-hes-tested-positive-for-covid-19.html (''Toronto Star'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in the United States]]
****The [[Food and Drug Administration|U.S. FDA]] issues a full approval for the [[Moderna COVID-19 vaccine]] for use in adults. [https://apnews.com/article/coronavirus-pandemic-moderna-vaccine-approved-dc6f5ac9eeb31667d5a28f0954335b65 (AP)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in India]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in India]]
***[[President of India|Indian President]] [[Ram Nath Kovind]] announces that 90% of adults in [[India]] have received their first dose of the [[COVID-19 vaccine]]. [https://theprint.in/india/90-pc-of-indias-adult-population-has-received-first-dose-of-covid-vaccine-prez/817683/ (''ThePrint'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Russia]]
***[[Russia]] reports a record for the 11th consecutive day of 124,070 new COVID-19 cases, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 11.86 million. [https://interfax.com/newsroom/top-stories/73752/ (Interfax)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in South Africa]]
***[[South Africa]] scraps the mandatory self-[[quarantine]] period for asymptomatic COVID-19 cases and cuts the mandatory self-quatantine period for symptomatic patients to seven days because 60% to 80% of its population now had COVID-19. [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2022-01-31/south-africa-eases-covid-19-rules-cuts-isolation-time (Bloomberg)]
*The [[Ecuador]]an environmental ministry reports that approximately {{convert|2|ha|acre}} of the [[Cayambe Coca Ecological Reserve]] have been contaminated following an [[oil spill]] attributed to a ruptured [[Pipeline transport|pipeline]]. [https://www.rfi.fr/en/oil-spill-pollutes-nature-reserve-in-ecuadoran-amazon (AFP via RFI)]

'''International relations'''
*[[France–Mali relations]]
**The [[Mali]]an [[military junta]] orders the [[France|French]] [[ambassador]] to leave the country within 72 hours in response to "outrageous comments" made by the French authorities about Mali's transitional government. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20220131-mali-authorities-give-french-ambassador-72-hours-to-leave-the-country (France 24)]
*[[2022 Burkinabé coup d'état]]
**The [[African Union]] suspends [[Burkina Faso]] in response to last week's [[coup d'état]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/african-union-suspends-burkina-faso-after-military-coup-2022-01-31/ (Reuters)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Murder of Ahmaud Arbery]]
**Gregory and Travis McMichael, two of the three people [[criminal conviction|convicted]] of [[murder (United States law)|murdering]] Ahmaud Arbery, have reached [[plea agreement]]s with federal prosecutors on [[hate crime]]s [[criminal charge|charges]]. However, U.S. District Court Judge Lisa Godbey Wood rejects the plea deal. [https://www.npr.org/2022/01/31/1076882516/two-of-the-men-convicted-of-murdering-ahmaud-arbery-have-reached-a-federal-plea- (NPR)] [https://apnews.com/article/ahmaud-arbery-crime-race-and-ethnicity-hate-crimes-savannah-4843bf04cf74034b2f396a844599f899?utm_campaign=SocialFlow&utm_medium=AP&utm_source=Twitter&s=09 (AP)]
*[[2022 Kusel shooting]]
**Two [[Law enforcement in Germany|police]] officers are shot dead during a routine traffic stop in [[Kusel (district)|Kusel]], [[Rhineland-Palatinate]], [[Germany]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-60195712 (BBC News)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[Partygate]]
**The initial findings of a report by senior [[civil service|civil servant]] [[Sue Gray (civil servant)|Sue Gray]] into allegations of rule breaking at [[10 Downing Street]] during [[COVID-19 lockdowns]] are published. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-politics-60195620 (BBC News)]
*[[Prime Minister of Peru|Peruvian Prime Minister]] [[Mirtha Vásquez]] [[resign]]s in response to a reshuffle of the [[government of Peru|government]] by [[President of Peru|President]] [[Pedro Castillo]]. [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2022-01-31/peru-prime-minister-quits-as-president-makes-changes-to-cabinet (Bloomberg)]
